newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil CS sugar output growth slows down - DataNet.
newsitem.headline: Brazil CS sugar output growth slows down - DataNet.

text.p: Sugar output in Brazil's center-south region showed a deceleration in growth in the tenth fortnightly period, giving a total rise of only 1.9 percent over the same period last year, said DataNet-Agricommodities.
This compares with a accumulated growth of 6.4 percent by the end of the ninth fortnightly period to September 1, the independent consultants said.
"It is possible that this is the start of a seasonal slowdown in production growth," DataNet said.
"DataNet will be conducting surveys to quantify the level of the slowdown from the eleventh fortnightly period," it added.

Actual sugar production by the end of the tenth period reached 7.14 million tonnes against 7.01 million tonnes in the corresponding period in the 1995/96 campaign which was up to September 1 as this year's harvest began two weeks earlier.
Sugar production by September 16, 1995 was 6.13 million tonnes, according to statistics from the Sao Paulo Association of Sugar and Alcohol Industries.
Cane crushings rose 2.2 percent to 158.16 million tonnes by the end of the tenth period against 154.69 million tonnes in the corresponding two-week period in 1995/96, DataNet said.
